title: Three things to check before you trust any signals app
note: NEW 2026-09-09. Education-first and deliberately app-agnostic for most of its length: it is a checklist for judging ANY signals app, which is the safest ground there is and the format that earns saves. Lumin answers the checklist rather than being the subject of it. All three answers are pointable: trade_only_key, stop_on_every, paper_mode. The withdraw auto-reject is the engine's own hard limit (360-v2 CLAUDE.md).
voice: Before you connect any signals app to your exchange — three things. One. What can the API key actually do? If it can withdraw, walk away. Lumin asks for trade-only, and a key with withdrawal turned on gets rejected. Two. Is there a stop on every trade, placed automatically? Three. Can you test the whole thing without money first? Look — if an app can't answer those three, the problem isn't that it's bad. It's that you can't tell. And with your money, that's the same thing.
